description: Flooding series, right-coded flooder. Participant A opens; then Participant B posts four short, civil messages in a row with no reply in between (messages 2 to 5; the trigger is message 5). Participant B is the right-coded side (against). Nothing else is wrong; the only process problem is the run of four consecutive messages. Mirrored across sides.

topic.title: Rent control
topic.proposition: Cities should cap how much landlords can raise rents each year.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: I support rent control, since housing is not an ordinary product. I think people cannot easily switch homes, and a sudden rent rise can force a family away from its neighborhood, its job and its children's school. A cap on annual rises gives tenants stability, and I think landlords can still earn a reasonable return. I think that trade is worth making, even though it is not free, and I would rather say so openly.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Stability is a fair goal, but I think a cap protects current tenants at others' expense.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Someone in a controlled apartment may have little reason to move.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Fewer units may then come on the market, and new renters face more competition and higher prices.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: That is why I would still favor vouchers.
